newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds hold on to gains, eye M3 data next week.
newsitem.headline: Bunds hold on to gains, eye M3 data next week.

text.p: German Bunds held on to their gains in late trade on Friday, underpinned by continued strength in U.S. Treasury prices and a favourable technical outlook, traders said.
December Bund futures were quoted at 99.56 at 1511 GMT, up 35 basis points from Thursday's close, after rising as high as 99.68 earlier in the session.
Dealers said they were confident the uptrend would continue next week, buoyed by an expected slowdown in M3 growth in September. The Bundesbank is expected to release M3 early next week.

Economists polled by Reuters forecast the annualised M3 growth slowed to a rate of between 8.2 percent and 8.5 percent in September after accelerating slightly to 8.7 percent in August from July's 8.6 percent.
But that slowdown is unlikely to strengthen the case for another rate cut, particularly in view of recent evidence that the economic recovery was well underway, economists said.
That was confirmed by Friday's September Ifo business climate index for west Germany, which rose to 95.7 from 94.4 in August.
But the Ifo index had little impact on Bunds because it was only slightly above forecasts of a figure ranging from 95 to 95.7.
